title: Returned-Fee Collection Share in a Patient Payment Plan Catch-Up
content:
**Training questions — returned-payment fees in the catch-up of a past-due Patient Payment Plan**

**At what share do returned-payment fees join the catch-up?**
Returned-payment fees of the current delinquency join the catch-up at a returned-fee collection share: for a plan signed at least 12 whole months before the handling date with exactly one returned-payment fee booked on installments within the last 12 months the share is 0.6, for such a plan with two or more the share is 0.8, and for any other plan the share is one. The returned-payment fees of the current delinquency are multiplied by this share as they join the catch-up.

**How is the plan's age measured?**
In whole calendar months from the date the agreement was signed to the handling date; 12 whole months or more meets the test.

**Which returned-payment fees are counted?**
Those booked on installments whose due dates lie within the last 12 months, that is, fewer than 12 whole calendar months before the handling date.

## Share by case

| Plan signed at least 12 whole months before the handling date | Returned-payment fees on installments within the last 12 months | Returned-fee collection share |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Exactly 1 | 0.6 |
| Yes | 2 or more | 0.8 |
| Yes | None | 1 |
| No | Any number | 1 |

## Hypothetical readings

- A plan signed 14 months before the handling date with one returned-payment fee of 25.00 in the delinquency and no other in the last 12 months: the fee joins as 15.00.
- The same plan with a second returned-payment fee earlier in the last 12 months: share 0.8, and the 25.00 joins as 20.00.
- A plan signed 11 whole months before the handling date: share one, whatever the count.
